classes.doc:
Actor is the base class for an Object that can be placed or spawned in a level.
Actors may contain a collection of ActorComponents, which can be used to control how actors move, how they are rendered, etc.
The other main function of an Actor is the replication of properties and function calls across the network during play.


Actor initialization has multiple steps, here's the order of important virtual functions that get called:
- UObject::PostLoad: For actors statically placed in a level, the normal UObject PostLoad gets called both in the editor and during gameplay.
                     This is not called for newly spawned actors.
- UActorComponent::OnComponentCreated: When an actor is spawned in the editor or during gameplay, this gets called for any native components.
                                       For blueprint-created components, this gets called during construction for that component.
                                       This is not called for components loaded from a level.
- AActor::PreRegisterAllComponents: For statically placed actors and spawned actors that have native root components, this gets called now.
                                    For blueprint actors without a native root component, these registration functions get called later during construction.
- UActorComponent::RegisterComponent: All components are registered in editor and at runtime, this creates their physical/visual representation.
                                      These calls may be distributed over multiple frames, but are always after PreRegisterAllComponents.
                                      This may also get called later on after an UnregisterComponent call removes it from the world.
- AActor::PostRegisterAllComponents: Called for all actors both in the editor and in gameplay, this is the last function that is called in all cases.
- AActor::PostActorCreated: When an actor is created in the editor or during gameplay, this gets called right before construction.
                            This is not called for components loaded from a level.
- AActor::UserConstructionScript: Called for blueprints that implement a construction script.
- AActor::OnConstruction: Called at the end of ExecuteConstruction, which calls the blueprint construction script.
                          This is called after all blueprint-created components are fully created and registered.
                          This is only called during gameplay for spawned actors, and may get rerun in the editor when changing blueprints.
- AActor::PreInitializeComponents: Called before InitializeComponent is called on the actor's components.
                                   This is only called during gameplay and in certain editor preview windows.
- UActorComponent::Activate: This will be called only if the component has bAutoActivate set.
                             It will also got called later on if a component is manually activated.
- UActorComponent::InitializeComponent: This will be called only if the component has bWantsInitializeComponentSet.
                                        This only happens once per gameplay session.
- AActor::PostInitializeComponents: Called after the actor's components have been initialized, only during gameplay and some editor previews.
- AActor::BeginPlay: Called when the level starts ticking, only during actual gameplay.
                     This normally happens right after PostInitializeComponents but can be delayed for networked or child actors.

@see https://docs.unrealengine.com/Programming/UnrealArchitecture/Actors
@see https://docs.unrealengine.com/Programming/UnrealArchitecture/Actors/ActorLifecycle
@see UActorComponent

A CameraActor is a camera viewpoint that can be placed in a level.

Controllers are non-physical actors that can possess a Pawn to control
its actions.  PlayerControllers are used by human players to control pawns, while
AIControllers implement the artificial intelligence for the pawns they control.
Controllers take control of a pawn using their Possess() method, and relinquish
control of the pawn by calling UnPossess().

Controllers receive notifications for many of the events occurring for the Pawn they
are controlling.  This gives the controller the opportunity to implement the behavior
in response to this event, intercepting the event and superseding the Pawn's default
behavior.

ControlRotation (accessed via GetControlRotation()), determines the viewing/aiming
direction of the controlled Pawn and is affected by input such as from a mouse or gamepad.

@see https://docs.unrealengine.com/latest/INT/Gameplay/Framework/Controller/

Info is the base class of an Actor that isn't meant to have a physical representation in the world, used primarily

A PlayerCameraManager is responsible for managing the camera for a particular
player. It defines the final view properties used by other systems (e.g. the renderer),
meaning you can think of it as your virtual eyeball in the world. It can compute the
final camera properties directly, or it can arbitrate/blend between other objects or
actors that influence the camera (e.g. blending from one CameraActor to another).

The PlayerCameraManagers primary external responsibility is to reliably respond to
various Get*() functions, such as GetCameraViewPoint. Most everything else is
implementation detail and overrideable by user projects.

By default, a PlayerCameraManager maintains a "view target", which is the primary actor
the camera is associated with. It can also apply various "post" effects to the final
view state, such as camera animations, shakes, post-process effects or special
effects such as dirt on the lens.

@see https://docs.unrealengine.com/latest/INT/Gameplay/Framework/Camera/

functions.name: DiffString
functions.doc:
Returns a string describing the LCS difference between two strings, First and Second.
This function is editor only because it is expensive for large strings. Examples:

("A", "") -> "- [ 0001 |      ] A"
("", "") -> ""
("The quick brown fox", "The quick red fox") -> "~ [ 0001 | 0001 ]
                  The quick brown fox
                            ~~~~~
                  The quick red   fox"

The numbers between the [], separated by |, are the line numbers in the First and Second string at
which the difference occurs. Preceding the line number information is a symbol identifying the type
of difference: A tilde (~) indicates a modification, a minus (-) indicates a removal from First, and
a plus (+) indicates an addition to second.

@param First - The string to treat as basis
@param Second - The string to treat as change
@return the LCS difference between the First and Second string

classes.doc:
The GameModeBase defines the game being played. It governs the game rules, scoring, what actors
are allowed to exist in this game type, and who may enter the game.

It is only instanced on the server and will never exist on the client.

A GameModeBase actor is instantiated when the level is initialized for gameplay in
C++ UGameEngine::LoadMap().

The class of this GameMode actor is determined by (in order) either the URL ?game=xxx,
the GameMode Override value set in the World Settings, or the DefaultGameMode entry set
in the game's Project Settings.

@see https://docs.unrealengine.com/latest/INT/Gameplay/Framework/GameMode/index.html

GameStateBase is a class that manages the game's global state, and is spawned by GameModeBase.
It exists on both the client and the server and is fully replicated.

PlayerControllers are used by human players to control Pawns.

ControlRotation (accessed via GetControlRotation()), determines the aiming
orientation of the controlled Pawn.

In networked games, PlayerControllers exist on the server for every player-controlled pawn,
and also on the controlling client's machine. They do NOT exist on a client's
machine for pawns controlled by remote players elsewhere on the network.

@see https://docs.unrealengine.com/latest/INT/Gameplay/Framework/Controller/PlayerController/

A PlayerState is created for every player on a server (or in a standalone game).
PlayerStates are replicated to all clients, and contain network game relevant information about the player, such as playername, score, etc.

PrimitiveComponents are SceneComponents that contain or generate some sort of geometry, generally to be rendered or used as collision data.
There are several subclasses for the various types of geometry, but the most common by far are the ShapeComponents (Capsule, Sphere, Box), StaticMeshComponent, and SkeletalMeshComponent.
ShapeComponents generate geometry that is used for collision detection but are not rendered, while StaticMeshComponents and SkeletalMeshComponents contain pre-built geometry that is rendered, but can also be used for collision detection.

@note The handle has game thread constraints related to UObjects and should be used carefully from other threads.

structs.doc: Structure containing information about one hit of a trace, such as point of impact and surface normal at that point.

fields.name: FaceIndex
fields.doc: Face index we hit (for complex hits with triangle meshes).

fields.name: Time
fields.doc:
'Time' of impact along trace direction (ranging from 0.0 to 1.0) if there is a hit, indicating time between TraceStart and TraceEnd.
For swept movement (but not queries) this may be pulled back slightly from the actual time of impact, to prevent precision problems with adjacent geometry.

fields.name: Distance
fields.doc: The distance from the TraceStart to the Location in world space. This value is 0 if there was an initial overlap (trace started inside another colliding object).

fields.name: Location
fields.doc:
The location in world space where the moving shape would end up against the impacted object, if there is a hit. Equal to the point of impact for line tests.
Example: for a sphere trace test, this is the point where the center of the sphere would be located when it touched the other object.
For swept movement (but not queries) this may not equal the final location of the shape since hits are pulled back slightly to prevent precision issues from overlapping another surface.

fields.name: ImpactPoint
Normal
fields.doc:
Normal of the hit in world space, for the object that was swept. Equal to ImpactNormal for line tests.
This is computed for capsules and spheres, otherwise it will be the same as ImpactNormal.
Example: for a sphere trace test, this is a normalized vector pointing in towards the center of the sphere at the point of impact.

fields.name: ImpactNormal
fields.doc:
Normal of the hit in world space, for the object that was hit by the sweep, if any.
For example if a sphere hits a flat plane, this is a normalized vector pointing out from the plane.
In the case of impact with a corner or edge of a surface, usually the "most opposing" normal (opposed to the query direction) is chosen.

fields.name: TraceStart
fields.doc:
Start location of the trace.
For example if a sphere is swept against the world, this is the starting location of the center of the sphere.

fields.name: TraceEnd
fields.doc:
End location of the trace; this is NOT where the impact occurred (if any), but the furthest point in the attempted sweep.
For example if a sphere is swept against the world, this would be the center of the sphere if there was no blocking hit.

fields.name: PenetrationDepth
fields.doc:
If this test started in penetration (bStartPenetrating is true) and a depenetration vector can be computed,
this value is the distance along Normal that will result in moving out of penetration.
If the distance cannot be computed, this distance will be zero.

fields.name: MyItem
fields.doc: If the hit result is from a collision this will have extra info about the item that hit the second item.

fields.name: Item
fields.doc: Extra data about item that was hit (hit primitive specific).

fields.name: ElementIndex
fields.doc: Index to item that was hit, also hit primitive specific.

fields.name: bBlockingHit
fields.doc: Indicates if this hit was a result of blocking collision. If false, there was no hit or it was an overlap/touch instead.

fields.name: bStartPenetrating
fields.doc:
Whether the trace started in penetration, i.e. with an initial blocking overlap.
In the case of penetration, if PenetrationDepth > 0.f, then it will represent the distance along the Normal vector that will result in
minimal contact between the swept shape and the object that was hit. In this case, ImpactNormal will be the normal opposed to movement at that location
(ie, Normal may not equal ImpactNormal). ImpactPoint will be the same as Location, since there is no single impact point to report.

fields.name: PhysMaterial
fields.doc:
Physical material that was hit.
@note Must set bReturnPhysicalMaterial on the swept PrimitiveComponent or in the query params for this to be returned.

fields.name: HitObjectHandle
fields.doc: Handle to the object hit by the trace.

fields.name: Component
fields.doc: PrimitiveComponent hit by the trace.

fields.name: BoneName
fields.doc: Name of bone we hit (for skeletal meshes).

fields.name: MyBoneName
fields.doc: Name of the _my_ bone which took part in hit event (in case of two skeletal meshes colliding).

fields.doc: Controls the color of the scene along the magenta - green axis (orthogonal to the color temperature).  This feature is equivalent to color tint in digital cameras.

fields.name: ColorSaturation
fields.doc: Control the intensity of the color(hue) for the entire image.Higher values will result in more vibrant colors.

fields.name: ColorContrast
fields.doc: Control the range of light and dark values in your scene. Lower values will reduce the difference between bright and dark areas while higher values will increase the difference between the bright and dark areas.

fields.name: ColorGamma
fields.doc: Control the luminance curve of the scene. Raising or lowering this value will result brightening or darkening the mid-tones of the entire image.

fields.name: ColorGain
fields.doc: This value multiplies the colors of the image.  Raising or lowering this value will result in brightening or darkening the entire scene.

fields.name: ColorOffset
fields.doc: This value is added to the colors of the scene.  Raising or lowering this value will result in the image being more or less washed-out.

fields.name: ColorSaturationShadows
fields.doc: Control the intensity of the colors (hue) in the shadow region of the image.  Higher values will result in more vibrant colors.

fields.name: ColorContrastShadows
fields.doc: Control the range of light and dark values in your scene. Lower values will reduce the difference between bright and dark areas while higher values will increase the difference between the bright and dark areas.

fields.name: ColorGammaShadows
fields.doc: Control the luminance curve of the shadow region. Raising or lowering this value will result brightening or darkening the mid-tones of the shadow region.

fields.name: ColorGainShadows
fields.doc: This value multiplies the colors in the shadow region.  Raising or lowering this value will result in brightening or darkening the affected region.

fields.name: ColorOffsetShadows
fields.doc: This value is added to the colors in the shadow region.  Raising or lowering this value will result in the shadows being more or less washed-out.

fields.name: ColorSaturationMidtones
fields.doc: Control the intensity of the colors (hue) in the mid-tone region of the image.  Higher values will result in more vibrant colors.

fields.name: ColorContrastMidtones
fields.doc: Control the range of light and dark values in the mid-tone region. Lower values will reduce the difference between bright and dark areas while higher values will increase the difference between the bright and dark areas.

fields.name: ColorGammaMidtones
fields.doc: Control the luminance curve of the mid-tone region of the image. Raising or lowering this value will result brightening or darkening the mid-tones of the image.

fields.name: ColorGainMidtones
fields.doc: This value multiplies the colors in the mid-tone region of the image.  Raising or lowering this value will result in brightening or darkening the affected region.

fields.name: ColorOffsetMidtones
fields.doc: This value is added to the colors in the mid-tone region of the image.  Raising or lowering this value will result in the mid-tones being more or less washed-out.

fields.name: ColorSaturationHighlights
fields.doc: Control the intensity of the color (hue) for the highlights region of the image.  Higher values will result in more vibrant colors.

fields.name: ColorContrastHighlights
fields.doc: Control the range of light and dark values in the highlights region. Lower values will reduce the difference between bright and dark areas while higher values will increase the difference between the bright and dark areas.

fields.name: ColorGammaHighlights
fields.doc: Control the luminance curve of the highlight region. Raising or lowering this value will result brightening or darkening the mid-tones of the highlight region.

fields.name: ColorGainHighlights
fields.doc: This value multiplies the colors in the highlight region.  Raising or lowering this value will result in brightening or darkening the affected region.

fields.name: ColorOffsetHighlights
fields.doc: This value is added to the colors in the highlight region.  Raising or lowering this value will result in the highlights being more or less washed-out.

fields.name: ColorCorrectionHighlightsMin
fields.doc: This value sets the lower threshold for what is considered to be the highlight region of the image.

fields.name: ColorCorrectionHighlightsMax
fields.doc: This value sets the upper threshold for what is considered to be the highlight region of the image.  This value should be larger than HighlightsMin. Default is 1.0, for backwards compatibility

fields.name: ColorCorrectionShadowsMax
fields.doc: This value sets the threshold for what is considered to be the shadow region of the image.

fields.name: BlueCorrection

fields.name: ExpandGamut
fields.doc: Expand bright saturated colors outside the sRGB gamut to fake wide gamut rendering.

fields.name: ToneCurveAmount
fields.doc: Allow effect of Tone Curve to be reduced (Set ToneCurveAmount and ExpandGamut to 0.0 to fully disable tone curve)

fields.name: TonemappingMethod
fields.doc: Controls the method of tonemapping.

fields.name: FilmSlope
fields.doc: Controls the overall steepness of the tonemapper curve.  Larger values increase scene contrast and smaller values reduce contrast.

fields.name: FilmToe
fields.doc: Controls the contrast of the dark end of the tonemapper curve. Larger values increase contrast and smaller values decrease contrast.

fields.name: FilmShoulder
fields.doc: Sometimes referred to as highlight rolloff.  Controls the contrast of the bright end of the tonemapper curve. Larger values increase contrast and smaller values decrease contrast.

fields.name: FilmBlackClip
fields.doc: Lowers the toe of the tonemapper curve by this amount. Increasing this value causes more of the scene to clip to black.  For most purposes, this property should remain 0

fields.name: FilmWhiteClip
fields.doc: Controls the height of the tonemapper curve.  Raising this value can cause bright values to more quickly approach fully-saturated white.

Diameter size for Bloom5 in percent of the screen width
(is done in 1/32 resolution, larger values cost more performance, best for wide contributions)
>=0: can be clamped because of shader limitations

fields.name: Bloom6Size
fields.doc:
Diameter size for Bloom6 in percent of the screen width
(is done in 1/64 resolution, larger values cost more performance, best for wide contributions)
>=0: can be clamped because of shader limitations

fields.name: Bloom1Tint
fields.doc: Bloom1 tint color

fields.name: Bloom2Tint
fields.doc: Bloom2 tint color

fields.name: Bloom3Tint
fields.doc: Bloom3 tint color

fields.name: Bloom4Tint
fields.doc: Bloom4 tint color

fields.name: Bloom5Tint
fields.doc: Bloom5 tint color

fields.name: Bloom6Tint
fields.doc: Bloom6 tint color

fields.name: BloomConvolutionIntensity
fields.doc: Multiplier for Convolution bloom contributions >=0: off, 1(default), >1 brighter

fields.name: BloomConvolutionScatterDispersion
fields.doc: Intensity multiplier on the scatter dispersion energy of the kernel. 1.0 means exactly use the same energy as the kernel scatter dispersion.

fields.name: BloomConvolutionSize
fields.doc: Relative size of the convolution kernel image compared to the minor axis of the viewport

fields.name: BloomConvolutionTexture
fields.doc: Texture to replace default convolution bloom kernel

fields.name: BloomConvolutionCenterUV
fields.doc: The UV location of the center of the kernel.  Should be very close to (.5,.5)

fields.name: BloomConvolutionPreFilterMin
fields.doc: Boost intensity of select pixels  prior to computing bloom convolution (Min, Max, Multiplier).  Max < Min disables

fields.name: BloomConvolutionPreFilterMax
fields.doc: Boost intensity of select pixels  prior to computing bloom convolution (Min, Max, Multiplier).  Max < Min disables

fields.name: BloomConvolutionPreFilterMult
fields.doc: Boost intensity of select pixels  prior to computing bloom convolution (Min, Max, Multiplier).  Max < Min disables

fields.name: BloomConvolutionBufferScale
fields.doc: Implicit buffer region as a fraction of the screen size to insure the bloom does not wrap across the screen.  Larger sizes have perf impact.

fields.name: BloomDirtMask
fields.doc: Texture that defines the dirt on the camera lens where the light of very bright objects is scattered.

fields.name: BloomDirtMaskIntensity
fields.doc: BloomDirtMask intensity

fields.name: BloomDirtMaskTint
fields.doc: BloomDirtMask tint color

fields.name: DynamicGlobalIlluminationMethod
fields.doc: Chooses the Dynamic Global Illumination method.  Not compatible with Forward Shading.

fields.name: IndirectLightingColor
fields.doc: Adjusts indirect lighting color. (1,1,1) is default. (0,0,0) to disable GI. The show flag 'Global Illumination' must be enabled to use this property.

fields.name: IndirectLightingIntensity
fields.doc: Scales the indirect lighting contribution. A value of 0 disables GI. Default is 1. The show flag 'Global Illumination' must be enabled to use this property.

fields.name: LumenRayLightingMode
fields.doc: Controls how Lumen rays are lit when Lumen is using Hardware Ray Tracing.  By default, Lumen uses the Surface Cache for best performance, but can be set to 'Hit Lighting' for higher quality.

fields.name: LumenSceneLightingQuality
fields.doc: Scales Lumen Scene's quality.  Larger scales cause Lumen Scene to be calculated with a higher fidelity, which can be visible in reflections, but increase GPU cost.

fields.name: LumenSceneDetail
fields.doc: Controls the size of instances that can be represented in Lumen Scene.  Larger values will ensure small objects are represented, but increase GPU cost.

fields.name: LumenSceneViewDistance
fields.doc: Sets the maximum view distance of the scene that Lumen maintains for ray tracing against.  Larger values will increase the effective range of sky shadowing and Global Illumination, but increase GPU cost.

fields.name: LumenSceneLightingUpdateSpeed
fields.doc: Controls how much Lumen Scene is allowed to cache lighting results to improve performance.  Larger scales cause lighting changes to propagate faster, but increase GPU cost.

fields.name: LumenFinalGatherQuality
fields.doc: Scales Lumen's Final Gather quality.  Larger scales reduce noise, but greatly increase GPU cost.

fields.name: LumenFinalGatherLightingUpdateSpeed
fields.doc: Controls how much Lumen Final Gather is allowed to cache lighting results to improve performance.  Larger scales cause lighting changes to propagate faster, but increase GPU cost and noise.

fields.name: LumenFinalGatherScreenTraces
fields.doc: Whether to use screen space traces for Lumen Global Illumination. Screen space traces bypass Lumen Scene and instead sample Scene Depth and Scene Color. This improves quality, as it bypasses Lumen Scene, but causes view dependent lighting.

fields.name: LumenMaxTraceDistance
fields.doc: Controls the maximum distance that Lumen should trace while solving lighting.  Values that are too small will cause lighting to leak into large caves, while values that are large will increase GPU cost.

fields.name: LumenDiffuseColorBoost
fields.doc: Allows brightening indirect lighting by calculating material diffuse color for indirect lighting. Values above 1 (original diffuse color) aren't physically correct, but they can be useful as an art direction knob to increase the amount of bounced light in the scene. Best to keep below 2 as it also causes reflections to be brighter than the scene.

fields.name: LumenAmbientOcclusionIntensity
fields.doc: Allows control over the strength of Lumen's Short Range Ambient Occlusion.

fields.name: LumenSkylightLeaking
fields.doc: Controls what fraction of the skylight intensity should be allowed to leak.  This can be useful as an art direction knob (non-physically based) to keep indoor areas from going fully black.

fields.name: LumenSkylightLeakingTint
fields.doc: Color tint for Lumen Skylight Leaking.

fields.name: LumenFullSkylightLeakingDistance
fields.doc: Controls the distance from a receiving surface where skylight leaking reaches its full intensity.  Smaller values make the skylight leaking flatter, while larger values create an Ambient Occlusion effect.

fields.name: LumenSurfaceCacheResolution
fields.doc: Scale factor for Lumen Surface Cache resolution.  Smaller values save GPU memory, at a cost in quality.  Defaults to 0.5 for Scene Captures if not overridden.

fields.name: ReflectionMethod
fields.doc: Chooses the Reflection method. Not compatible with Forward Shading.

fields.name: LumenReflectionQuality
fields.doc: Scales the Reflection quality.  Larger scales reduce noise in reflections, but increase GPU cost.

fields.name: LumenReflectionsScreenTraces
fields.doc: Whether to use screen space traces for Lumen Reflections. Screen space traces bypass Lumen Scene and instead sample Scene Depth and Scene Color. This improves quality, as it bypasses Lumen Scene, but causes view dependent lighting.

fields.name: LumenFrontLayerTranslucencyReflections
fields.doc: Whether to use high quality mirror reflections on the front layer of translucent surfaces.  Other layers will use the lower quality Radiance Cache method that can only produce glossy reflections.  Increases GPU cost when enabled.

fields.name: LumenMaxRoughnessToTraceReflections
fields.doc: Sets the maximum roughness value for which Lumen still traces dedicated reflection rays. Higher values improve reflection quality, but greatly increase GPU cost.

fields.name: LumenMaxReflectionBounces
fields.doc: Sets the maximum number of recursive reflection bounces. 1 means a single reflection ray (no secondary reflections in mirrors). Currently only supported by Hardware Ray Tracing with Hit Lighting.

fields.name: LumenMaxRefractionBounces
fields.doc: The maximum count of refraction event to trace. When hit lighting is used, Translucent meshes will be traced when LumenMaxRefractionBounces > 0, making the reflection tracing more expenssive.

fields.name: ScreenSpaceReflectionIntensity
fields.doc: Enable/Fade/disable the Screen Space Reflection feature, in percent, avoid numbers between 0 and 1 fo consistency

fields.name: ScreenSpaceReflectionQuality
fields.doc: 0=lowest quality..100=maximum quality, only a few quality levels are implemented, no soft transition, 50 is the default for better performance.

fields.name: ScreenSpaceReflectionMaxRoughness
fields.doc: Until what roughness we fade the screen space reflections, 0.8 works well, smaller can run faster

fields.name: bMegaLights
fields.doc:
Allows forcing MegaLights on or off for this volume, regardless of the project setting for MegaLights.
MegaLights will stochastically sample lights, which allows many shadow casting lights to be rendered efficiently, with a consistent and low GPU cost.
When MegaLights is enabled, other direct lighting algorithms like Deferred Shading will no longer be used, and other shadowing methods like Ray Traced Shadows, Distance Field Shadows and Shadow Maps will no longer be used.
MegaLights requires Hardware Ray Tracing and Shader Model 6.

fields.name: MegaLightsFrontLayerTranslucency
fields.doc: Whether to use high quality direct lighting on the front layer of translucent surfaces.  Other layers will use the lower quality Translucency Lighting Volume.  Increases GPU cost when enabled.

fields.name: AmbientCubemapTint
fields.doc: AmbientCubemap tint color

fields.name: AmbientCubemapIntensity
fields.doc:
To scale the Ambient cubemap brightness
>=0: off, 1(default), >1 brighter

fields.name: AmbientCubemap
fields.doc: The Ambient cubemap (Affects diffuse and specular shading), blends additively which if different from all other settings here

fields.name: CameraShutterSpeed
fields.doc: The camera shutter in 1/seconds.

fields.name: CameraISO
fields.doc: The camera sensor sensitivity

fields.name: DepthOfFieldFstop
fields.doc: Defines the opening of the camera lens, Aperture is 1/fstop, typical lens go down to f/1.2 (large opening), larger numbers reduce the DOF effect

fields.name: DepthOfFieldMinFstop
fields.doc: Defines the maximum opening of the camera lens to control the curvature of blades of the diaphragm. Set it to 0 to get straight blades.

fields.name: DepthOfFieldBladeCount
fields.doc: Defines the number of blades of the diaphragm within the lens (between 4 and 16).

fields.name: AutoExposureBias
fields.doc:
Logarithmic adjustment for the exposure. Only used if a tonemapper is specified.
0: no adjustment, -1:2x darker, -2:4x darker, 1:2x brighter, 2:4x brighter, ...

fields.name: AutoExposureBiasBackup
fields.doc:
With the auto exposure changes, we are changing the AutoExposureBias inside the serialization code. We are
storing that value before conversion here as a backup. Hopefully it will not be needed, and removed in the next engine revision.

fields.name: bOverride_AutoExposureBiasBackup
fields.doc:
With the auto exposure changes, we are also changing the auto exposure override value, so we are storing
that backup as well.

fields.name: AutoExposureApplyPhysicalCameraExposure
fields.doc: Only affects Manual exposure mode.

fields.name: AutoExposureBiasCurve
fields.doc:
Exposure compensation based on the scene EV100.
Used to calibrate the final exposure differently depending on the average scene luminance.
0: no adjustment, -1:2x darker, -2:4x darker, 1:2x brighter, 2:4x brighter, ...

fields.name: AutoExposureMeterMask
fields.doc:
Exposure metering mask. Bright spots on the mask will have high influence on auto-exposure metering
and dark spots will have low influence.

fields.name: AutoExposureLowPercent
fields.doc:
The eye adaptation will adapt to a value extracted from the luminance histogram of the scene color.
The value is defined as having x percent below this brightness. Higher values give bright spots on the screen more priority
but can lead to less stable results. Lower values give the medium and darker values more priority but might cause burn out of
bright spots.
>0, <100, good values are in the range 70 .. 80

fields.name: AutoExposureHighPercent
fields.doc:
The eye adaptation will adapt to a value extracted from the luminance histogram of the scene color.
The value is defined as having x percent below this brightness. Higher values give bright spots on the screen more priority
but can lead to less stable results. Lower values give the medium and darker values more priority but might cause burn out of
bright spots.
>0, <100, good values are in the range 80 .. 95

fields.name: AutoExposureMinBrightness
fields.doc:
Auto-Exposure minimum adaptation. Eye Adaptation is disabled if Min = Max.
Auto-exposure is implemented by choosing an exposure value for which the average luminance generates a pixel brightness equal to the Constant Calibration value.
The Min/Max are expressed in pixel luminance (cd/m2) or in EV100 when using ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange (see project settings).

fields.name: AutoExposureMaxBrightness
fields.doc:
Auto-Exposure maximum adaptation. Eye Adaptation is disabled if Min = Max.
Auto-exposure is implemented by choosing an exposure value for which the average luminance generates a pixel brightness equal to the Constant Calibration value.
The Min/Max are expressed in pixel luminance (cd/m2) or in EV100 when using ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange (see project settings).

fields.name: AutoExposureSpeedUp
fields.doc: In F-stops per second, should be >0

fields.name: AutoExposureSpeedDown
fields.doc: In F-stops per second, should be >0

fields.name: HistogramLogMin
fields.doc: Histogram Min value. Expressed in Log2(Luminance) or in EV100 when using ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange (see project settings)

fields.name: HistogramLogMax
fields.doc: Histogram Max value. Expressed in Log2(Luminance) or in EV100 when using ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange (see project settings)

fields.name: AutoExposureCalibrationConstant_DEPRECATED
fields.doc: Calibration constant for 18% albedo, deprecating this value.

fields.name: LocalExposureMethod
fields.doc: Local Exposure algorithm

fields.name: LocalExposureHighlightContrastScale
fields.doc:
Local Exposure decomposes luminance of the frame into a base layer and a detail layer.
Contrast of the base layer is reduced based on this value.
Value less than 1 will enable local exposure.
Good values are usually in the range 0.6 .. 1.0.

fields.name: LocalExposureShadowContrastScale
fields.doc:
Local Exposure decomposes luminance of the frame into a base layer and a detail layer.
Contrast of the base layer is reduced based on this value.
Value less than 1 will enable local exposure.
Good values are usually in the range 0.6 .. 1.0.

fields.name: LocalExposureHighlightContrastCurve
fields.doc:
Local Exposure Highlight Contrast based on the scene EV100.
Used to calibrate Local Exposure differently depending on the average scene luminance.

fields.name: LocalExposureShadowContrastCurve
fields.doc:
Local Exposure Shadow Contrast based on the scene EV100.
Used to calibrate Local Exposure differently depending on the average scene luminance.

fields.name: LocalExposureHighlightThreshold
fields.doc: Threshold used to determine which regions of the screen are considered highlights.

fields.name: LocalExposureShadowThreshold
fields.doc: Threshold used to determine which regions of the screen are considered shadows.

fields.name: LocalExposureDetailStrength
fields.doc:
Local Exposure decomposes luminance of the frame into a base layer and a detail layer.
Value different than 1 will enable local exposure.
This value should be set to 1 in most cases.

fields.name: LocalExposureBlurredLuminanceBlend
fields.doc:
Local Exposure decomposes luminance of the frame into a base layer and a detail layer.
Blend between bilateral filtered and blurred luminance as the base layer.
Blurred luminance helps preserve image appearance and specular highlights, and reduce ringing.
Good values are usually in the range 0.4 .. 0.6

fields.name: LocalExposureBlurredLuminanceKernelSizePercent
fields.doc: Kernel size (percentage of screen) used to blur frame luminance.

fields.name: LocalExposureHighlightThresholdStrength
fields.doc: Strength of the highlight threshold.

fields.name: LocalExposureShadowThresholdStrength
fields.doc: Strength of the shadow threshold.

fields.name: LocalExposureMiddleGreyBias
fields.doc:
Logarithmic adjustment for the local exposure middle grey.
0: no adjustment, -1:2x darker, -2:4x darker, 1:2x brighter, 2:4x brighter, ...

fields.name: LensFlareIntensity
fields.doc: Brightness scale of the image cased lens flares (linear)

fields.name: LensFlareTint
fields.doc: Tint color for the image based lens flares.

fields.name: LensFlareBokehSize
fields.doc: Size of the Lens Blur (in percent of the view width) that is done with the Bokeh texture (note: performance cost is radius*radius)

fields.name: LensFlareThreshold
fields.doc: Minimum brightness the lens flare starts having effect (this should be as high as possible to avoid the performance cost of blurring content that is too dark too see)

fields.name: LensFlareBokehShape
fields.doc: Defines the shape of the Bokeh when the image base lens flares are blurred, cannot be blended

fields.name: LensFlareTints
fields.doc: RGB defines the lens flare color, A it's position. This is a temporary solution.

fields.name: VignetteIntensity
fields.doc: 0..1 0=off/no vignette .. 1=strong vignette

fields.name: VignetteType
fields.doc: The shape type of the vignette

fields.name: VignetteCenter
fields.doc: Position of the vignette center in UV space.

fields.name: VignetteColor
fields.doc: Color multiplied with areas that are masked by the vignette. Default is black.

fields.name: VignetteSize
fields.doc: Scale of the vignette shape in screenspace. Can be used to scale vignette anamorphically. Default is 1.

fields.name: VignetteSoftness
fields.doc: The softness of the transition from opaque to transparant on the edge of the vignette shape.

fields.name: VignetteTexture
fields.doc: Defines the shape of the vignette when VignetteType is set to Texture

fields.name: Sharpen
fields.doc: Controls the strength of image sharpening applied during tonemapping.

fields.name: FilmGrainIntensity
fields.doc: 0..1 Film grain intensity to apply. LinearSceneColor *= lerp(1.0, DecodedFilmGrainTexture, FilmGrainIntensity)

fields.name: FilmGrainIntensityShadows
fields.doc: Control over the grain intensity in the regions of the image considered shadow areas.

fields.name: FilmGrainIntensityMidtones
fields.doc: Control over the grain intensity in the mid-tone region of the image.

fields.name: FilmGrainIntensityHighlights
fields.doc: Control over the grain intensity in the regions of the image considered highlight areas.

fields.name: FilmGrainShadowsMax
fields.doc: Sets the upper bound used for Film Grain Shadow Intensity.

fields.name: FilmGrainHighlightsMin
fields.doc: Sets the lower bound used for Film Grain Highlight Intensity.

fields.name: FilmGrainHighlightsMax
fields.doc: Sets the upper bound used for Film Grain Highlight Intensity. This value should be larger than HighlightsMin.. Default is 1.0, for backwards compatibility

fields.name: FilmGrainScale
fields.doc: Controls the size of the film grain. Size of texel of FilmGrainTexture on screen.

fields.name: FilmGrainTexture
fields.doc: Defines film grain texture to use.

fields.name: AmbientOcclusionIntensity
fields.doc: 0..1 0=off/no ambient occlusion .. 1=strong ambient occlusion, defines how much it affects the non direct lighting after base pass

fields.name: AmbientOcclusionStaticFraction
fields.doc: 0..1 0=no effect on static lighting .. 1=AO affects the stat lighting, 0 is free meaning no extra rendering pass

fields.name: AmbientOcclusionRadius
fields.doc: >0, in unreal units, bigger values means even distant surfaces affect the ambient occlusion

fields.name: AmbientOcclusionRadiusInWS
fields.doc: true: AO radius is in world space units, false: AO radius is locked the view space in 400 units

fields.name: AmbientOcclusionFadeDistance
fields.doc: >0, in unreal units, at what distance the AO effect disppears in the distance (avoding artifacts and AO effects on huge object)

fields.name: AmbientOcclusionFadeRadius
fields.doc: >0, in unreal units, how many units before AmbientOcclusionFadeOutDistance it starts fading out

fields.name: AmbientOcclusionDistance_DEPRECATED
fields.doc: >0, in unreal units, how wide the ambient occlusion effect should affect the geometry (in depth), will be removed - only used for non normal method which is not exposed

fields.name: AmbientOcclusionPower
fields.doc: >0, in unreal units, bigger values means even distant surfaces affect the ambient occlusion

fields.name: AmbientOcclusionBias
fields.doc: >0, in unreal units, default (3.0) works well for flat surfaces but can reduce details

fields.name: AmbientOcclusionQuality
fields.doc: 0=lowest quality..100=maximum quality, only a few quality levels are implemented, no soft transition

fields.name: AmbientOcclusionMipBlend
fields.doc: Affects the blend over the multiple mips (lower resolution versions) , 0:fully use full resolution, 1::fully use low resolution, around 0.6 seems to be a good value

fields.name: AmbientOcclusionMipScale
fields.doc: Affects the radius AO radius scale over the multiple mips (lower resolution versions)

fields.name: AmbientOcclusionMipThreshold
fields.doc: to tweak the bilateral upsampling when using multiple mips (lower resolution versions)

fields.name: AmbientOcclusionTemporalBlendWeight
fields.doc: How much to blend the current frame with previous frames when using GTAO with temporal accumulation

fields.name: RayTracingAO
fields.doc: Enables ray tracing ambient occlusion.

fields.name: RayTracingAOSamplesPerPixel
fields.doc: Sets the samples per pixel for ray tracing ambient occlusion.

fields.name: RayTracingAOIntensity
fields.doc: Scalar factor on the ray-tracing ambient occlusion score.

fields.name: RayTracingAORadius
fields.doc: Defines the world-space search radius for occlusion rays.

fields.name: ColorGradingIntensity
fields.doc: Color grading lookup table intensity. 0 = no intensity, 1=full intensity

fields.name: ColorGradingLUT
fields.doc: Look up table texture to use or none of not used

fields.name: DepthOfFieldEnabled
fields.doc: When false, post-process depth of field will not be used. When true, DoF may be used depending on lens and scalability settings.

fields.name: DepthOfFieldSensorWidth
fields.doc: Width of the camera sensor to assume, in mm.

fields.name: DepthOfFieldSqueezeFactor
fields.doc: This is the squeeze factor for the DOF, which emulates the properties of anamorphic lenses.

fields.name: DepthOfFieldFocalDistance
fields.doc: Distance in which the Depth of Field effect should be sharp, in unreal units (cm)

fields.name: DepthOfFieldDepthBlurAmount
fields.doc: CircleDOF only: Depth blur km for 50%

fields.name: DepthOfFieldDepthBlurRadius
fields.doc: CircleDOF only: Depth blur radius in pixels at 1920x

fields.name: DepthOfFieldUseHairDepth
fields.doc: For depth of field to use the hair depth for computing circle of confusion size. Otherwise use an interpolated distance between the hair depth and the scene depth based on the hair coverage (default).

fields.name: DepthOfFieldPetzvalBokeh
fields.doc: Simulate stretching in blur and bokeh. Positive values for sagittal (swirly bokeh), negative values for tangential.

fields.name: DepthOfFieldPetzvalBokehFalloff
fields.doc: How quickly does the Petzval bokeh effect increase towards the edge of the image

fields.name: DepthOfFieldPetzvalExclusionBoxExtents
fields.doc: Box, centered on screen, around which the Petzval effect is applied.

fields.name: DepthOfFieldPetzvalExclusionBoxRadius
fields.doc: Corner radius

fields.name: DepthOfFieldAspectRatioScalar
fields.doc: Amount to scale the output viewport's aspect ratio by when computing depth of field properties.

fields.name: DepthOfFieldBarrelRadius
fields.doc: The lens barrel creates vignetting and occludes bokeh, i.e. cat's eye bokeh

fields.name: DepthOfFieldBarrelLength
fields.doc: The lens barrel creates vignetting and occludes bokeh, i.e. cat's eye bokeh

fields.name: DepthOfFieldMatteBoxFlags
fields.doc: Panels around the front of the lens barrel that occlude bokeh

fields.name: DepthOfFieldFocalRegion
fields.doc: Artificial region where all content is in focus, starting after DepthOfFieldFocalDistance, in unreal units  (cm)

fields.name: DepthOfFieldNearTransitionRegion
fields.doc: To define the width of the transition region next to the focal region on the near side (cm)

fields.name: DepthOfFieldFarTransitionRegion
fields.doc: To define the width of the transition region next to the focal region on the near side (cm)

fields.name: DepthOfFieldScale
fields.doc:
SM5: BokehDOF only: To amplify the depth of field effect (like aperture)  0=off
          ES3_1: Used to blend DoF. 0=off

fields.name: DepthOfFieldNearBlurSize
fields.doc: Gaussian only: Maximum size of the Depth of Field blur (in percent of the view width) (note: performance cost scales with size)

fields.name: DepthOfFieldFarBlurSize
fields.doc: Gaussian only: Maximum size of the Depth of Field blur (in percent of the view width) (note: performance cost scales with size)

fields.name: DepthOfFieldOcclusion
fields.doc: Occlusion tweak factor 1 (0.18 to get natural occlusion, 0.4 to solve layer color leaking issues)

fields.name: DepthOfFieldSkyFocusDistance
fields.doc: Artificial distance to allow the skybox to be in focus (e.g. 200000), <=0 to switch the feature off, only for GaussianDOF, can cost performance

fields.name: DepthOfFieldVignetteSize
fields.doc: Artificial circular mask to (near) blur content outside the radius, only for GaussianDOF, diameter in percent of screen width, costs performance if the mask is used, keep Feather can Radius on default to keep it off

fields.name: MotionBlurAmount
fields.doc: Strength of motion blur, 0:off

fields.name: MotionBlurMax
fields.doc: max distortion caused by motion blur, in percent of the screen width, 0:off

fields.name: MotionBlurTargetFPS
fields.doc:
Defines the target FPS for motion blur. Makes motion blur independent of actual frame rate and relative
to the specified target FPS instead. Higher target FPS results in shorter frames, which means shorter
shutter times and less motion blur. Lower FPS means more motion blur. A value of zero makes the motion
blur dependent on the actual frame rate.

fields.name: MotionBlurPerObjectSize
fields.doc: The minimum projected screen radius for a primitive to be drawn in the velocity pass, percentage of screen width. smaller numbers cause more draw calls, default: 4%

fields.name: TranslucencyType
fields.doc: Sets the translucency type

fields.name: RayTracingTranslucencyMaxRoughness
fields.doc: Sets the maximum roughness until which ray tracing translucency will be visible (lower value is faster). Translucency contribution is smoothly faded when close to roughness threshold. This parameter behaves similarly to ScreenSpaceReflectionMaxRoughness.

fields.name: RayTracingTranslucencyRefractionRays
fields.doc: Sets the maximum number of ray tracing refraction rays.

fields.name: RayTracingTranslucencySamplesPerPixel
fields.doc: Sets the samples per pixel for ray traced translucency.

fields.name: RayTracingTranslucencyMaxPrimaryHitEvents
fields.doc: Maximum number of hit events allowed on primary ray paths

fields.name: RayTracingTranslucencyMaxSecondaryHitEvents
fields.doc: Maximum number of hit events allowed on secondary ray paths

fields.name: RayTracingTranslucencyShadows
fields.doc: Sets the translucency shadows type.

fields.name: RayTracingTranslucencyRefraction
fields.doc: Sets whether refraction should be enabled or not (if not rays will not scatter and only travel in the same direction as before the intersection event).

fields.name: RayTracingTranslucencyUseRayTracedRefraction
fields.doc: Whether to use ray traced refraction which currently doesn't work well with rough refraction or simulate it using a screen space effect

fields.name: PathTracingMaxBounces
fields.doc: Sets the path tracing maximum bounces

fields.name: PathTracingSamplesPerPixel
fields.doc: Sets the samples per pixel for the path tracer.

fields.name: PathTracingMaxPathIntensity
fields.doc: Sets the maximum intensity of indirect samples to reduce fireflies. Lowering this value reduces noise at the expense of accuracy. Increasing it is more accurate but may lead to more noise.

fields.name: PathTracingEnableEmissiveMaterials
fields.doc: Should emissive materials contribute to scene lighting?

fields.name: PathTracingEnableReferenceDOF
fields.doc: Enables a reference quality depth-of-field which replaces the post-process effect.

fields.name: PathTracingEnableReferenceAtmosphere
fields.doc: Enables path tracing in the atmosphere instead of baking the sky atmosphere contribution into a skylight. Any skylight present in the scene will be automatically ignored when this is enabled.

fields.name: PathTracingEnableDenoiser
fields.doc: Run the currently loaded denoiser plugin on the last sample to remove noise from the output. Has no effect if a plug-in is not loaded.

fields.name: PathTracingIncludeEmissive
fields.doc: Should the render include directly visible emissive elements?

fields.name: PathTracingIncludeDiffuse
fields.doc: Should the render include diffuse lighting contributions?

fields.name: PathTracingIncludeIndirectDiffuse
fields.doc: Should the render include indirect diffuse lighting contributions?

fields.name: PathTracingIncludeSpecular
fields.doc: Should the render include specular lighting contributions?

fields.name: PathTracingIncludeIndirectSpecular
fields.doc: Should the render include indirect specular lighting contributions?

fields.name: PathTracingIncludeVolume
fields.doc: Should the render include volume lighting contributions?

fields.name: PathTracingIncludeIndirectVolume
fields.doc: Should the render include volume lighting contributions?

fields.name: UserFlags
fields.doc: Per-view user flags accessible in materials via TestPostVolumeUserFlag node, allowing per-view overrides of material behavior.

fields.name: WeightedBlendables
fields.doc:
Allows custom post process materials to be defined, using a MaterialInstance with the same Material as its parent to allow blending.
For materials this needs to be the "PostProcess" domain type. This can be used for any UObject object implementing the IBlendableInterface (e.g. could be used to fade weather settings).

fields.name: PreviewBlendable
fields.doc:
For editor material preview windows, we need to support visualizing the output of a blendable that writes to a UserSceneTexture.  Stores
a pointer to a blendable that's being previewed, forcing its output to write to SceneColor instead of the UserSceneTexture, making it visible.
